paragraphs: Friend, I know a list of names looks like the part of the Bible where you check your phone. But look at what David is doing here. He is setting up order for the house of the LORD, and the priests get twenty-four families and twenty-four turns. Nothing about serving God was left to chance or to whoever shoved to the front.

Now watch how the turns get handed out. They cast lots in the presence of the king, and Eleazar's bigger side and Ithamar's smaller side go into the same drawing. The reason is that there were "officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both" (1 Chronicles 24:5). Then the other Levite families do it too, and the family heads and their "younger brothers alike" (1 Chronicles 24:31) all cast lots. Big family, small family, oldest, youngest, everybody gets a place.

Here's what that means for you, baker. Serving God is not a spot reserved for the biggest names. Every family on that list had a turn, and every name was written down in front of the king. Also, this order followed what "the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded" Aaron (1 Chronicles 24:19), so it was never just David's bright idea. Your turn to serve is real and it counts, and I'm saying that as a stamper who once sat in a drawer thinking nobody would ever call his number.
